Figure 1:Left:Policies with (π0.5\pi_{0.5}& X-VLA) and
without large-scale action pretraining (“w/o PT” & VLA-Adapter-Pro)
perform similarly on standard benchmarks (LIBERO-Spatial & Object), while
larger gaps emerge on long-horizon tasks (LIBERO-10), under
perturbations (LIBERO-Plus), and on the real-world Pick Beverage task.
These results motivate transferring capabilities from pretrained EFMs to
student policies without repeating action pretraining.Right:(a)
Offline distillation is restricted to the demonstration distribution, leading
to distribution mismatch during student execution. (b) On-Policy
Distillation extends supervision to student-induced states but does not
execute teacher corrections to observe the subsequent recovery states. (c)
Human-in-the-loop methods collect recovery trajectories through human monitoring
and intervention, but their coverage is limited by the bandwidth of
human supervision. (d) TILDE jointly learns from demonstration,
student-induced rollout, and failure recovery distributions, with AutoDAgger automating progress monitoring and teacher intervention for efficient
data collection.

Figure 2:AutoDAgger pipeline.A reward-model-based task monitor
estimates task progress and success probability. The execution manager
uses these signals to coordinate policy execution, trigger teacher intervention
upon detected student failure, and select successful recovery episodes
for data aggregation. Pre-intervention student rollout and successful teacher
recovery are recorded without human monitoring or takeover.Bottom:A real-world Fold Dishcloth example; green/blue denote student/teacher
execution, while red marks the detected failure and intervention point.

Figure 7:Representative AutoDAgger collection trajectories.Examples
for Fold Dishcloth, Pick Pen, and Pick Beverage are shown from top to bottom.
Green, red, and blue frame borders denote student execution, detected failure,
and teacher recovery, respectively. The red dashed line marks the success
thresholdθs=0.5\theta_{s}=0.5.
